blocks.title: A Fool Shows Everyone He is a Fool

texts.NIV84: As dead flies give perfume a bad smell, so a little folly outweighs wisdom and honor.
texts.KJV: Dead flies cause the ointment of the apothecary to send forth a stinking savour: so doth a little folly him that is in reputation for wisdom and honour.
texts.DRB: Dying flies spoil the sweetness of the ointment. Wisdom and glory is more precious than a small and shortlived folly.

texts.NIV84: The heart of the wise inclines to the right, but the heart of the fool to the left.
texts.KJV: A wise man's heart is at his right hand; but a fool's heart at his left.
texts.NKJV:
A wise man’s heart is at his right hand,
But a fool’s heart at his left.
texts.DRB: The heart of a wise man is in his right hand, and the heart of a fool is in his left hand.

texts.NIV84: Even as he walks along the road, the fool lacks sense and shows everyone how stupid he is.
texts.KJV: Yea also, when he that is a fool walketh by the way, his wisdom faileth him, and he saith to every one that he is a fool.
texts.NKJV:
Even when a fool walks along the way,
He lacks wisdom,
And he shows everyone that he is a fool.
texts.DRB: Yea, and the fool when he walketh in the way, whereas be himself is a fool, esteemeth all men fools.

texts.NIV84: If a ruler's anger rises against you, do not leave your post; calmness can lay great errors to rest.
texts.KJV: If the spirit of the ruler rise up against thee, leave not thy place; for yielding pacifieth great offences.
texts.DRB: If the spirit of him that hath power, ascend upon thee, leave not thy place: because care will make the greatest sins to cease.

blocks.title: An Error Proceeding From a Ruler

texts.NIV84: There is an evil I have seen under the sun, the sort of error that arises from a ruler:
texts.KJV: There is an evil which I have seen under the sun, as an error which proceedeth from the ruler:
texts.NKJV:
There is an evil I have seen under the sun,
As an error proceeding from the ruler:
texts.DRB: There is an evil that I have seen under the sun, as it were by an error proceeding from the face of the prince:

texts.NIV84: Fools are put in many high positions, while the rich occupy the low ones.
texts.KJV: Folly is set in great dignity, and the rich sit in low place.
texts.NKJV:
Folly is set in great dignity,
While the rich sit in a lowly place.
texts.DRB: A fool set in high dignity, and the rich sitting beneath.

texts.NIV84: I have seen slaves on horseback, while princes go on foot like slaves.
texts.KJV: I have seen servants upon horses, and princes walking as servants upon the earth.
texts.NKJV:
I have seen servants on horses,
While princes walk on the ground like servants.
texts.DRB: I have seen servants upon horses: and princes walking on the ground as servants.

blocks.title: Those Who Dig a Pit Will Fall Into It

texts.NIV84: Whoever digs a pit may fall into it; whoever breaks through a wall may be bitten by a snake.
texts.KJV: He that diggeth a pit shall fall into it; and whoso breaketh an hedge, a serpent shall bite him.
texts.NKJV:
He who digs a pit will fall into it,
And whoever breaks through a wall will be bitten by a serpent.
texts.DRB: He that diggeth a pit, shall fall into it: and he that breaketh a hedge, a serpent shall bite him.

texts.NIV84: Whoever quarries stones may be injured by them; whoever splits logs may be endangered by them.
texts.KJV: Whoso removeth stones shall be hurt therewith; and he that cleaveth wood shall be endangered thereby.
texts.NKJV:
He who quarries stones may be hurt by them,
And he who splits wood may be endangered by it.
texts.DRB: He that removeth stones, shall be hurt by them: and he that cutteth trees, shall be wounded by them.

texts.NIV84: If the ax is dull and its edge unsharpened, more strength is needed but skill will bring success.
texts.KJV: If the iron be blunt, and he do not whet the edge, then must he put to more strength: but wisdom is profitable to direct.
texts.NKJV:
If the ax is dull,
And one does not sharpen the edge,
Then he must use more strength;
But wisdom brings success.
texts.DRB: If the iron be blunt, and be not as before, but be made blunt, with much labour it shall be sharpened: and after industry shall follow wisdom.

blocks.title: A Blabber is Like the Bite of a Serpent

texts.NIV84: If a snake bites before it is charmed, there is no profit for the charmer.
texts.KJV: Surely the serpent will bite without enchantment; and a babbler is no better.
texts.NKJV:
A serpent may bite when it is not charmed;
The babbler is no different.
texts.DRB: If a serpent bite in silence, he is nothing better that backbiteth secretly.

texts.NIV84: Words from a wise man's mouth are gracious, but a fool is consumed by his own lips.
texts.KJV: The words of a wise man's mouth are gracious; but the lips of a fool will swallow up himself.
texts.NKJV:
The words of a wise man’s mouth are gracious,
But the lips of a fool shall swallow him up;
texts.DRB: The words of the mouth of a wise man are grace: but the lips of a fool shall throw him down headlong.

texts.NIV84: At the beginning his words are folly; at the end they are wicked madness-
texts.KJV: The beginning of the words of his mouth is foolishness: and the end of his talk is mischievous madness.
texts.NKJV:
The words of his mouth begin with foolishness,
And the end of his talk is raving madness.
texts.DRB: The beginning of his words is folly, and the end of his talk is a mischievous error.

texts.NIV84: and the fool multiplies words. No one knows what is coming- who can tell him what will happen after him?
texts.KJV: A fool also is full of words: a man cannot tell what shall be; and what shall be after him, who can tell him?
texts.DRB: A fool multiplieth words. A man cannot tell what hath been before him: and what shall be after him, who can tell him?

texts.NIV84: A fool's work wearies him; he does not know the way to town.
texts.KJV: The labour of the foolish wearieth every one of them, because he knoweth not how to go to the city.
texts.NKJV:
The labor of fools wearies them,
For they do not even know how to go to the city!
texts.DRB: The labour of fools shall afflict them that know not how to go to the city.

blocks.title: Do Not Curse the King in Thought

texts.NIV84: Woe to you, O land whose king was a servant and whose princes feast in the morning.
texts.KJV: Woe to thee, O land, when thy king is a child, and thy princes eat in the morning!
texts.NKJV:
Woe to you, O land, when your king is a child,
And your princes feast in the morning!
texts.DRB: Woe to thee, O land, when thy king is a child, and when the princes eat in the morning.

texts.NIV84: Blessed are you, O land whose king is of noble birth and whose princes eat at a proper time- for strength and not for drunkenness.
texts.KJV: Blessed art thou, O land, when thy king is the son of nobles, and thy princes eat in due season, for strength, and not for drunkenness!
texts.NKJV:
Blessed are you, O land, when your king is the son of nobles,
And your princes feast at the proper time—
For strength and not for drunkenness!
texts.DRB: Blessed is the land, whose king is noble, and whose princes eat in due season for refreshment, and not for riotousness.

texts.NIV84: If a man is lazy, the rafters sag; if his hands are idle, the house leaks.
texts.KJV: By much slothfulness the building decayeth; and through idleness of the hands the house droppeth through.
texts.NKJV:
Because of laziness the building decays,
And through idleness of hands the house leaks.
texts.DRB: By slothfulness a building shall be brought down, and through the weakness of hands, the house shall drop through.

texts.NIV84: A feast is made for laughter, and wine makes life merry, but money is the answer for everything.
texts.KJV: A feast is made for laughter, and wine maketh merry: but money answereth all things.
texts.DRB: For laughter they make bread, and wine that the living may feast: and all things obey money.

texts.NIV84: Do not revile the king even in your thoughts, or curse the rich in your bedroom, because a bird of the air may carry your words, and a bird on the wing may report what you say.
texts.KJV: Curse not the king, no not in thy thought; and curse not the rich in thy bedchamber: for a bird of the air shall carry the voice, and that which hath wings shall tell the matter.
texts.DRB: Detract not the king, no not in thy thought; and speak not evil of the rich man in thy private chamber: because even the birds of the air will carry thy voice, and he that hath wings will tell what thou hast said.
